scores.reason: Point estimate about 3,000,000 adults per year (range 650,000 to 6,500,000): MASLD 86.3 million US adults in 2020 (model output, PMID 39821400; the paper gives no share with type 2 diabetes); share without T2D about 75 percent [assumption, about 65 million]; share newly suspected or evaluated each year about 5 percent [assumption, range 1 to 10 percent]. Fasting-based (HOMA-IR) in the guideline population (adults with suspected MASLD, no T2D). Alternative bin 4 if fewer than about 1.5 percent of this pool (under 1,000,000) are evaluated in a year; that share decides it.

EASL-EASD-EASO 2024: HOMA-IR or OGTT estimates 'may be considered to clarify metabolic dysfunction in adults with (suspected) MASLD and without an established diagnosis of type 2 diabetes' (LoE 3, weak, consensus); the population matches. Option-level, so 2. Measure: fasting-based HOMA-IR (OGTT-derived alternative named). The AASLD 2023 guidance has no such recommendation (project skeptic result, not rechecked here); a multisociety Delphi consensus co-led by US bodies (PMID 37364790 DOI 10.1016/j.jhep.2023.06.003, project files, abstract level) says suspected cases 'may' prompt HOMA-IR, so I count it as 2 for the US. Under a strict reading of clarification 6 (European guideline only) it would be 1.
sources: PMID 38852583 DOI 10.1159/000539371 full text (PMC11299976, keyword windows; same EASL-EASD-EASO 2024 guideline as PMIDs 38851997 DOI 10.1016/j.jhep.2024.04.031 and 38869512 DOI 10.1007/s00125-024-06196-3)

scores.reason: Narrowest population (clarification 2): evaluation of beta-cell reserve in candidates for total pancreatectomy with islet autotransplantation (TPIAT), where PancreasFest applies C-peptide. TP+IAT procedures in the US rose from 53 (2002) to 155 (2012) per year (NIS, PMID 27011922); no later count was found. Assume 250 to 400 procedures now and 2 to 3 candidates evaluated per operation: point estimate about 800 (range 300 to 1,500). C-peptide, fasting or stimulated. Alternative bin 2 if evaluated candidates exceed 1,000, i.e. more than about 3 evaluations per procedure. Broader note: new pancreatogenic diabetes (classification use) is about 5,000 to 30,000 a year (chronic pancreatitis incidence 4 to 12 per 100,000 per year, AAFP 2018 page; pooled cumulative incidence of any diabetes about 30 percent over follow-up, PMID 42488134 (18 percent under 5 years, 44 percent over 10; not confirmed type 3c and not an annual share); acute pancreatitis about 82 per 100,000 adults per year, PMID 30946239), bin 3, not scored.
sources: PMID 27011922 DOI 10.5500/wjt.v6.i1.233 abstract (as returned by web search)
AAFP 2018 'Chronic Pancreatitis: Diagnosis and Treatment' https://www.aafp.org/afp/2018/0315/p385 excerpt

scores.reason: PancreasFest 2012 consensus (US): 'Assessment of pancreatic endocrine reserve, and importantly that of functional beta-cell mass, should be performed as part of the evaluation and followup for TPIAT', estimated from serum C-peptide during OGTT or mixed-meal test. A consensus recommendation in the specific population, so 3; not 4 because it is a consensus with 58 percent top agreement and no label or guideline requires it. It does not recommend C-peptide for diagnosing type 3c diabetes in general (that is glucose-based). Measure: C-peptide, post-load or mixed-meal.
sources: PMID 23890130 DOI 10.1016/j.pan.2013.05.002 full text (PMC3830751, keyword windows)

scores.reason: Narrowest population: adults with diabetes and eGFR below 60 in whom C-peptide classification is considered. New diagnosed adult diabetes 1.21 million per year (CDC NDSR, 2019 to 2021 crude, 1,094 to 1,328 thousand); share with eGFR below 60 about 10 percent [assumption; CKD of any kind is 37 percent of adults with diabetes, CDC KDSS, but that includes albuminuria]; share with a C-peptide-based classification question about 10 percent [assumption, range 3 to 25 percent]. Point estimate about 12,000 (range 4,000 to 30,000). Alternative bin 2 if the share is under about 8 percent. Prevalent patients retested (about 5 million with diabetes and CKD) not counted. C-peptide (serum or urinary).
sources: CDC National Diabetes Statistics Report (restored copy 2024-05-15) https://restoredcdc.org/www.cdc.gov/diabetes/php/data-research/index.html , incidence 1,211 thousand, 2019-2021; CDC Kidney Disease Surveillance System Q763 https://wwwn.cdc.gov/kdss/detail.aspx?Qnum=Q763&topic=4 (37.0 percent CKD among adults with diabetes, 2017-March 2020); USRDS ADR 2022 ch.1

scores.reason: No US guideline retrieved that addresses C-peptide interpretation or adjustment in CKD; searches 'C-peptide chronic kidney disease eGFR guideline interpretation type 1 diabetes' and 'C-peptide diabetes kidney disease eGFR cutoff classification' returned 0 records. The project files record KDIGO 2022 as blank at abstract level. The only text is a review (Jones and Hattersley 2013, PMID 23413806) calling renal correction methods poorly validated; a review is not a guideline. Not addressed, so 1. Measure: C-peptide.
sources: PMID 23413806 DOI 10.1111/dme.12159 full text (via project files, keyword windows)

scores.reason: Narrowest population: patients worked up for suspected severe or syndromic IR (lipodystrophy, genetic IR, type B). Registry prevalence: generalized 1.6 and partial 6.4 per million (France, PMID 40174859), about 8 per million, so about 2,700 prevalent lipodystrophy patients in the US (340 million) [extrapolation, registry undercount likely]; type B has about 119 published cases worldwide in a 2020 review (PMID 32813762). Patients in whom the question arises (clarification 4) are larger than those diagnosed: assume 2 new work-ups for each prevalent-equivalent diagnosed per year, point estimate about 5,000 (range 1,000 to 20,000). Alternative bin 3 if more than 10,000 are worked up. Fasting insulin.

The US-endorsed multisociety lipodystrophy guideline (Brown 2016) says all lipodystrophy patients 'should undergo a metabolic workup for insulin resistance, diabetes, dyslipidemia, and fatty liver disease' but names no insulin assay, threshold or antibody test; the condition is named, the measurement is not (clarification 5), so 2. The Japanese JDS criteria (fasting insulin above 30 uU/mL, PMID 35463863) are national criteria elsewhere and count as 1 for the US (clarification 6); no US or international body adoption found. Measure: fasting insulin (JDS); unspecified (Brown).
sources: PMID 27710244 DOI 10.1210/jc.2016-2466 full text (PMC5155679, keyword windows)
PMID 35463863 DOI 10.1007/s13340-022-00570-5 full text (PMC8980125, via project files)

scores.reason: Situation (clarification 4): adults without diabetes drugs worked up for spontaneous hypoglycaemia in whom insulin and C-peptide come back suppressed. Hypoglycaemia in non-diabetic admissions 36 per 10,000 admissions (StatPearls summarising one retrospective review of 38,898 admissions, secondary source); about 33 million US admissions [recall, no source retrieved] gives roughly 120,000 episodes; share with a formal insulin and C-peptide work-up and suppressed result about 8 percent [assumption, range 3 to 20 percent]. Point estimate about 10,000 (range 3,000 to 25,000). Alternative bin 2 if the share is below 8 percent. NICTH itself is far rarer (solitary fibrous tumour 2.8 per 100,000, about 5 to 10 percent with hypoglycaemia, PMID 34413033, abstract). Measure: insulin plus C-peptide (fasting or during symptoms). Confidence low: boundary estimate and a recall input.
scores.correction: 2026-10-23, main session, after skeptic V19: the chain gives about 9,500 per year (bin 2); the 33 million admissions figure is recalled; alternative bin 3, confidence low

scores.reason: The Endocrine Society hypoglycaemia guideline (Cryer 2009, PMID 19088155 DOI 10.1210/jc.2008-1410) recommends measuring insulin, C-peptide and related variables during hypoglycaemia in adults without diabetes; this is a broader population than the use case (suppressed values to redirect to NICTH work-up), and IGF-II is the confirmatory test, so 2 (clarification 14). Full text could not be retrieved (no PMC copy); status rests on the abstract and project files. Measure: insulin and C-peptide, spontaneous or fasting-test.
sources: PMID 19088155 DOI 10.1210/jc.2008-1410 abstract/title only (no PMC copy)

scores.reason: Situation: adults with ketoacidosis soon after hyperglycaemic symptoms and near-normal HbA1c at new diagnosis, in whom C-peptide would be used. US DKA hospitalisations about 200,000 or more a year (Diabetes Care 2020 update, 220,340 cases in the first column year of its table; exact year not verified); share of adult DKA that is a new diagnosis about 15 percent [assumption]; share with HbA1c below 8.7 percent and abrupt onset about 4 percent [assumption]. Point estimate about 1,500 (range 300 to 5,000). Fulminant T1D incidence outside Japan was not found (PubMed 'fulminant type 1 diabetes C-peptide criteria guideline' 0 records). Alternative bin 3 if the share exceeds about 30 percent of new-onset DKA, which is unlikely. Broader count (all new-onset DKA, about 30,000) is bin 3, noted not scored. C-peptide (urinary or serum, fasting and stimulated).

The criteria (urinary C-peptide below 10 ug/day, or fasting serum C-peptide below 0.3 ng/mL and below 0.5 ng/mL after glucagon or meal) are Japan Diabetes Society national criteria (PMID 24843620 DOI 10.1111/jdi.12024, PMC4015434); no US or international body adoption found in the screened records, so 1 (clarification 6). Measure: C-peptide.
sources: PMID 24843620 DOI 10.1111/jdi.12024 abstract (full text read by project skeptic)

scores.reason: Scored for the insulin-based part, first-trimester HOMA-IR in pregnancy. Pregnant women without pre-existing diabetes: 3,596,017 US births in 2023 (NVSR 74-1) and 1.2 percent prepregnancy diabetes, so about 3.5 million (range 3.3 to 3.6 million). Fasting-based (HOMA-IR). The GCK-testing branch is glucose-based and not scored; for reference 296,661 GDM births in 2023 (NVSR 74-1) times about 6 percent referred by the NSC criteria (PMID 26109503) is about 18,000 (bin 3).

anchor_issues: Row 9 D7 and D3: the use case has two decisions (document insulin deficiency in type 3c; beta-cell reserve before TPIAT). I scored the TPIAT evaluation, the only decision for which a consensus names C-peptide (clarification 2, narrowest). The type 3c classification count (bin 3) is a note.
Row 35: the row mixes a glucose-based GCK trigger (a) and first-trimester HOMA-IR (b). I scored (b) only because (a) does not use insulin or C-peptide.

Row 14 D3: rule 6 (non-US national criteria count 1) is unclear for a multisociety European guideline. I counted the EASL-EASD-EASO guideline as 2 because a US-co-led Delphi consensus points the same way; strict reading gives 1.
Row 12 D3: rule 5 (condition named but not test, score 2) conflicts with D3 anchor 1 (not addressed) when the guideline asks for an 'insulin resistance workup' without naming a test. I chose 2.
D7 for rows 28, 21, 46 and 14 depends on 'share evaluated' factors that no source gives; per rule 24 I scored the point-estimate bin with low confidence and stated the alternative bin.
Rule 4 (count the situation, not the diagnosis) and rule 2 (narrowest population) pull in different directions for row 9; narrowest was used.

Share of MASLD with T2D about 25 percent; share evaluated or newly suspected each year about 5 percent (row 14).

New-onset diabetes with eGFR below 60 about 10 percent, C-peptide question in 10 percent (row 28).
